I forgot my password. How do I reset it?
cases.answer: Use the self‑service reset first: go to https://id.halcyon-dynamics.example/reset and enter your work email, verify with your registered MFA method (Authenticator app or FIDO2 key), choose a new password that meets the requirements, and then sign out and back in on all devices to avoid lockouts [1][2][1]. Self‑service reset requires that you have already enrolled in MFA; if you have never set up MFA, contact the Service Desk instead [1]. If you cannot use self‑service, call the Service Desk on extension 4357 or visit the walk‑up IT desk; the analyst will verify your identity using your employee ID and a callback to the phone number in the HR system and will provide a temporary password that must be changed at first sign‑in [3].

judge.explanation: The answer's steps and contact details match the provided KB sources and the reference; all factual claims are present in the cited sources and it includes the key points from the reference.

cases.question: How long does my new password have to be?
cases.answer: Your new password must be at least 14 characters long [1][2].

judge.explanation: The answer matches the sources which state the minimum length is 14 characters, and it matches the reference key fact.

cases.question: My account got locked after I typed the wrong password a few times. What should I do?
cases.answer: Wait 15 minutes — accounts are locked for 15 minutes after 5 failed sign‑in attempts and the lock clears automatically, so you do not need to raise a ticket [1]. After the lock clears, sign in with the correct password and sign out and back in on all devices (including your phone email app) to avoid further lockouts [2][1]. Check for old saved credentials (for example on phones or mapped drives) and update or remove them after every password change, since those commonly cause repeated lockouts [1]. If you believe your password was exposed or you entered it on a suspicious site, reset it immediately using self‑service and then report it as a security incident via Security > Report a Phishing or Compromise in the portal [3][2].

judge.explanation: All factual claims are present in the provided sources, and the answer includes the reference's key facts (15-minute automatic unlock, no ticket needed, and update saved credentials) without contradiction.

cases.question: Can I use SMS text messages as my MFA method?
cases.answer: No — SMS text messages are not permitted as an MFA method; SMS is listed as Not permitted due to vulnerability to SIM‑swap attacks [1]. Use an approved method instead, for example Microsoft Authenticator (push + number matching), a FIDO2 hardware security key, or the 6‑digit authenticator code (TOTP) as a fallback [1].

judge.explanation: The answer's statements match the provided source and the reference: SMS is not permitted (SIM‑swap risk) and approved alternatives are Microsoft Authenticator push, FIDO2 hardware keys, and the 6‑digit authenticator code.

cases.question: I lost the phone that has my Authenticator app. How can I sign in?
cases.answer: Call the Service Desk on extension 4357; after identity verification the analyst can issue a Temporary Access Pass (valid for 8 hours) so you can register a new MFA method [1]. Use the portal (https://id.halcyon-dynamics.example/security) to add your Authenticator app again: Add sign-in method > Authenticator app, then scan the QR code in the Microsoft Authenticator app and complete the approval/number-matching step [2][1]. Alternatively, you can request a FIDO2 security key from the Service Desk and register it via Add sign-in method > Security key (insert/tap key, create PIN, name the key) [3][1]. We recommend registering a second method so you won’t be locked out in future [3]; do not use SMS or voice call methods (not permitted) [4].

judge.explanation: The answer's instructions (call Service Desk for an 8‑hour Temporary Access Pass, re-register Microsoft Authenticator via the security portal, optionally request/register a FIDO2 key, and avoid SMS/voice) are all stated in the provided sources and match the reference guidance.

cases.question: How do I connect to the VPN on my Windows laptop?
cases.answer:
1. Ensure you have an active Halcyon ID with MFA enrolled and a working internet connection; company-managed laptops already have SecureLink installed and personal devices aren’t permitted to connect [1].
2. Click the SecureLink shield icon in the system tray; if it’s missing, open Start > SecureLink [2].
3. Confirm the gateway is set to vpn.halcyon-dynamics.example [2].
4. Click Connect and sign in with your Halcyon ID email and password [2].
5. Approve the push notification in Microsoft Authenticator or tap your FIDO2 security key (or use the 6-digit code if push doesn’t arrive) [2][1].
6. The SecureLink shield icon turns green and the status shows Connected – Full Tunnel when connected [2].
7. If you cannot reach the gateway, accept any Wi‑Fi captive portal in a browser or try the fallback gateway vpn-tcp.halcyon-dynamics.example; if the device isn’t enrolled you may see a “Certificate not trusted” error and must contact the Service Desk [1].

unsupported_claims: You can use the 6-digit MFA code if the push doesn’t arrive (not stated in the sources).
Try the fallback gateway vpn-tcp.halcyon-dynamics.example if you cannot reach the gateway (not stated in the sources).
If the device isn’t enrolled you may see a “Certificate not trusted” error and must contact the Service Desk (the exact certificate error and contact instruction are not stated in the sources).
judge.explanation: The answer’s core connection steps match the sources, but it adds a few specifics (6-digit code fallback, a named fallback gateway, and a certificate-error/contact instruction) that are not present in the provided sources. Compared to the reference, the answer contains the required key steps and thus is correct.

cases.question: SecureLink says 'gateway unreachable' when I'm in a hotel. What can I do?
cases.answer: If SecureLink reports “Gateway unreachable” from a hotel, the VPN is often blocked by the Wi‑Fi captive portal or a firewall; open a browser and accept the hotel’s Wi‑Fi portal to allow the VPN through [1][2]. If that doesn’t work, switch SecureLink to use the TCP fallback gateway `vpn-tcp.halcyon-dynamics.example` (this avoids UDP 4501 being blocked) [1].

judge.explanation: The answer's claims (captive portal/firewall blocking, accept portal in browser, use the TCP fallback gateway to avoid UDP 4501 being blocked) are all stated in the provided sources and match the reference.

cases.question: My VPN keeps disconnecting every few minutes on my MacBook. Is there a fix?
cases.answer: This is a known issue on macOS 15 and a vendor fix is expected in SecureLink 6.4; status: Open with a workaround available [1]. The problem is caused by a macOS 15 power-management change that sleeps the network extension on battery when the screen is locked, interrupting VPN keepalive, and symptoms include drops after 3–10 minutes with a ‘tunnel keepalive timeout’ in the SecureLink log [2][3]. Workaround (follow these steps): 1) Open System Settings > Battery > Options and turn on “Prevent automatic sleeping on power adapter when the display is off” [4]. 2) Turn off “Enable Power Nap” [4]. 3) In SecureLink, go to Settings > Connection and change the protocol from Auto to TCP (uses vpn-tcp.halcyon-dynamics.example) [4]. 4) Disconnect and reconnect the VPN; most users report the TCP setting alone stops the disconnects [4]. If the drops continue after the workaround, raise a ticket under Network > VPN, mention KI-0007, and attach the SecureLink log (Help > Export Logs); tickets for this known issue are handled as P3 [5].

judge.explanation: The answer accurately restates the sources: it describes the macOS 15 power-management cause, symptoms, the Open status and expected vendor fix in SecureLink 6.4, lists the battery and SecureLink TCP workaround steps, and the ticketing guidance; all claims are present in the provided sources and match the reference.

cases.question: Can I connect my personal laptop to the company VPN?
cases.answer: No — personal laptops are not permitted to connect to the company VPN; only company-managed devices may connect to the VPN, Halcyon-Corp Wi‑Fi, or internal systems [1][2]. Personal phones and tablets may only access email and Teams through the Outlook and Teams mobile apps after registering on Halcyon-BYOD, per the Acceptable Use Policy [2].

judge.explanation: The answer accurately states that personal laptops cannot use the company VPN and correctly adds policy details about Wi‑Fi/internal systems and mobile app access; all claims are present in the provided sources and align with the reference.

cases.question: Nobody can hear me in Teams calls when my ThinkPad is on the docking station.
cases.answer: This is a known issue where other participants can’t hear you when a ThinkPad is connected to a Lenovo USB‑C Dock Gen 2; audio works when undocked and the problem began after the September Windows update [1]. After the update Windows can select the dock’s audio as the default device and Teams follows Windows’ default, causing the issue [2]. Workaround: in the Teams call click More (…) > Settings > Device settings and explicitly select your headset under Speaker and Microphone instead of “Default device” [3]. To make it permanent, open Windows Settings > System > Sound and set your headset as the default input and output device [3]. If the headset is not listed, unplug the dock, wait 10 seconds, and plug it back in [3]. A firmware update for the docking stations is being tested and will be deployed automatically, and the issue is currently open with a workaround available [4]. If the workaround does not resolve the problem, raise a ticket under Collaboration > Teams Issue and mention KI‑0012 and the dock serial number from the underside of the dock [5].

judge.explanation: The answer restates the issue, cause, workaround steps, firmware status, and ticket instructions exactly as given in the provided sources and matches the reference's key facts.

cases.question: Outlook is stuck on 'Loading Profile'. How do I fix it?
cases.answer:
1. Close Outlook completely, including from the system tray [1].
2. Start Outlook in safe mode: press Windows + R, type outlook.exe /safe, and press Enter [1].
3. If Outlook opens in safe mode, disable recently added COM add-ins via File > Options > Add-ins (remove the faulty add-in) [1].
4. If safe mode also fails, create a new mail profile: Control Panel > Mail > Show Profiles > Add, then set the new profile as the default [1].

judge.explanation: The answer restates the steps from the reference and exactly matches the provided source KB-0005, covering safe mode, disabling COM add-ins, and creating a new mail profile as needed.

cases.question: What is the maximum size of an email I can send?
cases.answer: Messages larger than 35 MB including attachments are rejected, so the maximum size you can send is 35 MB [1].

cases.question: How big is my mailbox, and what happens when it fills up?
cases.answer: Standard mailboxes have a 100 GB quota and an online archive is available to every user with an additional 100 GB [1]. When the mailbox reaches 98% full you can no longer send email; to free space empty Deleted Items and Junk Email, search for large items (search box: size:>10MB), or enable/use the online archive [1].

judge.explanation: The answer matches the source and includes the same key facts as the reference: 100 GB mailbox, 98% send restriction, ways to free space, and 100 GB online archive.

cases.question: How do I add the office printer on my Mac?
cases.answer: Make sure you are connected to the office network (Halcyon‑Corp Wi‑Fi or wired) or to the VPN [1]. Open System Settings > Printers & Scanners > Add Printer [2]. Select the IP tab and enter print01.halcyon-dynamics.example, set Protocol to LPD, Queue to HD-FollowMe, and use Generic PostScript as the driver [2].

cases.question: How do I get a new laptop, and how long does delivery take?

Select the profile you need and (for Power and Mac profiles) provide a business justification, then submit—the request is routed to your manager for approval [1]. After manager approval, standard models are delivered within 5 business days [1][2]. If you request non‑standard hardware it requires approval from both your manager and the End User Computing lead and can take up to 20 business days for delivery [2].

cases.question: Which Wi-Fi network should I use for my personal phone in the office?
cases.answer: Use Halcyon-BYOD for your personal phone and tablet in the office [1][2]. cases.question: My company laptop won't connect to the office Wi-Fi.
cases.answer: If your company laptop won’t connect, note that managed laptops should connect to Halcyon-Corp automatically using a device certificate [1][2]. 1) Turn Wi‑Fi off and on, then try again [1]. 2) Restart the laptop while in the office so the device certificate can renew [1]. 3) If the laptop has been away from the office and off VPN for more than 90 days the certificate may have expired; connect with a network cable or the VPN once, then restart [1]. 4) Move closer to an access point (meeting rooms with closed doors can have weaker signal) and check https://status.halcyon-dynamics.example for a Wi‑Fi incident at your site [3]. 5) If problems persist, report it under Network > WiFi Issue and include your office, floor and the time the problem happened [3].

judge.explanation: All claims in the answer are present in the provided sources, and the answer includes the reference's key troubleshooting steps without contradiction.

cases.question: How do I get access to the Finance shared drive?
cases.answer:
Request access via the Service Desk portal: select Access > Shared Drive Access and enter the full folder path (for example \\files.halcyon-dynamics.example\Finance\Reports) then choose Read or Read/Write and give a business reason (requests without a reason are returned). [1][2][1]
The data owner (usually the department head) approves or rejects the request; access is granted within 2 business days of approval. [2][1]
If the Finance folder contains Confidential or Restricted data you will also need Security team approval and access will be reviewed every 90 days. [3]
After approval sign out of Windows and sign back in, then disconnect and remap the drive if needed; if access still fails after 4 hours reply to your request ticket. [4]
To map the drive on Windows open File Explorer > This PC > Map network drive, pick a letter, enter the folder path and tick Reconnect at sign-in; on macOS use Finder > Go > Connect to Server and enter smb://files.halcyon-dynamics.example/Finance. You must be on the corporate network or connected to the VPN (shared drives are not available on Halcyon-BYOD or Halcyon-Guest Wi‑Fi). [5][5]

judge.explanation: The answer's steps and details are all stated in the provided sources and it includes the key facts from the reference (how to request, required fields, approver, and timing).

cases.question: I'm starting next week. What do I need to do in my first week for IT?
cases.answer:
1) Sign in to the laptop with the username and temporary password from your manager's welcome email on day one and change your password when prompted (minimum 14 characters). [1]
2) Enrol in MFA — you must do this within 7 days. [1]
3) Open Outlook and Teams and confirm they load. [1]
4) Connect to the VPN once if you are working remotely. [1]
5) Complete the mandatory Security Awareness training in the learning portal within 14 days (access to sensitive systems is withheld until it is done). [2]
6) Read and accept the Acceptable Use Policy (POL-0001). [2]
7) Install any role-specific software from the Company Portal (see KB-0008). [2]
8) Request access to shared drives your team uses (see KB-0011). [2]
9) If you will print in the office, register your building badge on a printer. [2]
10) Note: your Halcyon ID account, mailbox and a standard laptop are created/shipped if your manager submitted a New Starter Request at least 10 business days before your start date. [3]

judge.explanation: The answer's steps and timelines are all present in the provided sources and it includes the reference's key items; no unsupported claims or missing reference points were found.

cases.question: Am I allowed to paste customer data into ChatGPT to summarise it?
cases.answer: No — you must not paste customer personal data into public ChatGPT; the policy states customer personal data and source code must never be entered into public AI chatbots [1]. Customer data is classed as Confidential, and Confidential/Restricted data have strict handling rules (Confidential access limited; Restricted more tightly controlled), so you may only use AI tools approved by the Security team and listed in the Company Portal for company data [2][1].

2) You already have an open ticket for this: INC-1001 (VPN disconnects every few minutes on MacBook), status in_progress — I won't create a duplicate.

Workaround (from the KB): Open SecureLink → Settings > Connection, change the protocol from Auto to TCP (this uses the fallback gateway vpn-tcp.halcyon-dynamics.example). Then disconnect and reconnect the VPN. [1]
